sources.title: Fourier transforms of positive definite kernels and the Riemann xi-Function
sources.inspection: Selected statements and the full-line normalization in (3.11)–(3.14) checked. Pólya's convex-kernel criterion and the associated-kernel characterization are used as classical tools. Section 4.6 switches to a half-line transform; this review derives constants from the full-line statement instead of copying (4.7).
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Sections 2 and 5: separate the convex primitive criterion from positive definiteness of associated kernels. The latter is stronger than pointwise positivity.

followup_inspections.detail: Theorem 2.4 and expansion (2.11), Theorem 3.7, Section 4 coefficient normalization, and Open Problem 4.14 rechecked for implication directions. Example 3.12 noted as a related Gaussian-polynomial diagnostic.

sources.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and the Turan Inequalities
sources.inspection: Selected primary pages inspected as rendered images because the PDF is scanned. The integrated kernel is K(t)=integral from t to infinity of Phi(sqrt(u)) du. It is not the manuscript's psi_theta. The proof treats moment indices at least two analytically and the first separately; the full 21-page proof was not audited.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 4: the principal precedent for integrating first and then proving a stronger shape inequality. K is explicitly distinguished from p and G.

followup_inspections.detail: Printed pp. 523–527 visually inspected: integrated kernel and determinant-composition mechanism; full Section 3 and Section 4 not audited.

sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 6: a possible change of basis with positive coefficients. No real-rootedness conclusion is imported from coefficient signs alone.

sources.title: Jensen polynomials for the Riemann zeta function and other sequences
sources.inspection: Fixed-degree eventual hyperbolicity and its Hermite limit checked. The sufficiently large shift depends on degree. This does not establish the all-degrees/all-shifts RH criterion and is not a uniform statement about physical heat time.

sources.relevance: Section 4: a subsequent coefficient-based result with a fixed-degree quantifier, distinct from a global all-degrees conclusion.

followup_inspections.detail: Introduction and definition of Jensen polynomials: all d,n hyperbolicity, and sufficiency of all degrees at n=0.

Rechecked introduction, sufficiency of every degree at shift zero by differentiation, and Theorem 1 fixed-degree eventual-shift quantifiers. No all-degree improvement claimed.

sources.title: Second-Level Concavity of the Riemann Xi Kernel
checked_passages: Theorem 1.1; Sections 2–3; selected Sections 5.1 and 5.5–5.7; Sections 6–8
sources.relevance: Reports log-concavity of the first differential Laguerre expression of s(t)=Phi(sqrt(t)). Two methods: theta first-term/tail estimates and Jacobi differential dynamics with a cone barrier.
sources.limitations: Preprint claim, selected arguments inspected; certificates not rerun and full proof not audited. Source-coordinate concavity and double coefficient Turan inequalities, not the spectral first Laguerre inequality or RH.

followup_inspections.detail: Continuation read Sections 5.1–5.7: Jacobi system and initial data, kernel factorization, elliptic ratio, clock/quartic reduction and first-contact/monotonicity architecture. Selected algebra reconstructed in Note02; certificates not rerun and full proof not independently audited.

Rechecked primary HTML (5.10)-(5.12): canonical Jacobi orbit, initial data and source reconstruction. The proposed derivative-ratio curvature sign is not an imported consequence; second-concavity theorem/certificates remain unaudited.

sources.title: Infinite log-concavity of the Taylor coefficients of the Riemann xi-function
checked_passages: Introduction; Theorem 1.1; Section 2, equations (2.1)–(2.4); proof architecture and appendix contents
sources.relevance: Reports strict infinite log-concavity of ordinary coefficients lambda_n of xi(1/2+sqrt(x)). Uses logarithmic-ratio recurrences, saddle estimates, finite interval verification and closure.
sources.limitations: Preprint claim, not independently verified; code not executed. Ordinary lambda_n must be distinguished from exponential coefficients n! lambda_n. This is not all Jensen hyperbolicity or RH.

sources.title: The Jensen–Pólya program and inequalities for arithmetic sequences

sources.limitations: Discovery and setup inspection, not a theorem import. Applications discussed concern partition-type sequences; the hypotheses have not been verified for this investigation's primitive moments.

sources.title: Jensen polynomials for the Riemann xi-function
checked_passages: Section 1, Theorems 1.1–1.2 and Corollary 1.3; Section 2, Lemma 2.4 and start of proof
sources.relevance: Makes eventual Jensen hyperbolicity effective: n >= c exp(d/2). A Hermite-basis coefficient criterion supplies an explicit sufficient error budget.
sources.limitations: Version v3 read, journal version not separately compared. Degree-dependent threshold persists; verified-zero implications are one-way, not a new primitive noncollision estimate.

followup_inspections.detail: Theorem 1.1 and Remarks 1.2/1.3: effective large-shift region and limitations of finite zero/Jensen implications.
Rechecked primary HTML coefficient convention and Theorems 1.1-1.2: n >= c exp(d/2) and the finite-degree consequence of verified zeros. No full proof audit.

sources.title: Certain Extensions of Results of Siegel, Wilton and Hardy
checked_passages: Introduction and Theorem 1.1; Definitions 1.1–1.3; modular relation (1.29)
sources.relevance: Extends the theta/Hardy mechanism through Bessel and modified Bessel transformation formulas to specified Hecke-functional-equation Dirichlet series.
sources.limitations: Selected setup and statements only. Absolute summability, bounded distinct shifts attaining their bounds, and the stated auxiliary-parameter domain matter. Infinitely many critical-line zeros, not all zeros real.

sources.title: Estimates for the number of zeros of shifted combinations of completed Dirichlet series
checked_passages: Theorem 1.1; discussion of Fekete/Fejer method; Remark 1.2 and equation (1.28)
sources.relevance: Quantifies critical-line zero production for a specified class of shifted combinations; the z=0 specialization has a lower bound of order sqrt(T)/log(T).
sources.limitations: Selected statements and method description, not a full proof audit. Retain summable real coefficients, bounded shifts, symmetry assumptions and parameter restrictions. Not an improvement to the ordinary zeta critical-zero proportion.

sources.title: Zeros of Jensen polynomials and asymptotics for the Riemann xi function
sources.version: arXiv:2007.13582v2, 9 December 2020; Research in the Mathematical Sciences 8 (2021), article 46
checked_passages: Introduction, equations (1.1)–(1.4) and Theorems 1.1–1.2; section outline
sources.relevance: Introduces Hermite-weighted polynomial combinations and detailed xi coefficient asymptotics; useful companion to the effective Jensen result.
sources.limitations: Selected introductory passages; no new asymptotic bound imported. Its Hermite-weighted P^{d,n} differs from ordinary J^{d,n}. Its citation of an earlier effective threshold should not replace Griffin et al. v3.

sources.title: Jensen polynomials are not a plausible route to proving the Riemann Hypothesis
sources.relevance: Interpretive counterweight: generic differentiation/Hermite universality must be distinguished from theta-specific evidence about RH.
sources.limitations: Abstract and outline inspection only. The strategic assessment is the author's argument, not an impossibility theorem against every coefficient method.

followup_inspections.detail: Sections 3–4 selected discussion of Hermite universality and loss of zero information under differentiation; interpretive caution, not a universal impossibility theorem.
